Teacher Curriculum · Grades 9–10

Geometry

Discover how geometry explains mountain bike design, trail construction, angles, jumps, distances, and three-dimensional objects.

4 quarters · 9 units · 43 topics · 11 lesson plans ready

Proposed sequence This quarter-by-quarter order is Mathlete MTB’s suggested pacing for a typical school year, not a school’s confirmed calendar. Your school’s order may differ; every lesson stands on its own.

Quarter 1 Aug – Oct Plans coming Quarter 2 Nov – Jan · Now 11 lesson plans Quarter 3 Jan – Mar Plans coming Quarter 4 Apr – Jun Plans coming

Quarter 1Points, lines, angles and proof

Aug – Oct · 2 units · 8 topics · lesson plans in development

  1. Unit 1 Foundations of Geometry 4 topics
    1. 1.1

      Points, Lines, and Planes

      Use the undefined terms of geometry and the notation for naming figures.

      Lesson plan planned Student topic page
    2. 1.2

      Segments and Angles

      Measure and construct segments and angles; use the segment and angle addition postulates.

      Lesson plan planned Student topic page
    3. 1.3

      Angle Relationships

      Complementary, supplementary, vertical and linear-pair angles.

      Lesson plan planned Student topic page
    4. 1.4

      Parallel and Perpendicular Lines

      Angles formed by a transversal, and conditions that make lines parallel or perpendicular.

      Lesson plan planned Student topic page
  2. Unit 2 Reasoning and Proof 4 topics
    1. 2.1

      Logical Reasoning

      Inductive and deductive reasoning, and counterexamples.

      Lesson plan planned Student topic page
    2. 2.2

      Conditional Statements

      If-then statements, their converse, inverse and contrapositive, and biconditionals.

      Lesson plan planned Student topic page
    3. 2.3

      Geometric Proofs

      Write two-column and paragraph proofs using definitions, postulates and theorems.

      Lesson plan planned Student topic page
    4. 2.4

      Congruence Statements

      Write congruence statements and use corresponding parts.

      Lesson plan planned Student topic page
